method: Same decision-point replay, but on a SINGLE-PROMPT segment of transcript 400budnp: the one user prompt 'Analyse the data of ReixachGCO' drives a 96-tool-call autonomous run (msgs 0..224, before the first follow-up). 8 decision points sampled across it. Three tool-description regimes compared on the IDENTICAL 8 points: FULL (shipped, 27.5K chars), FIRST-SENTENCE (2.0K, 93% cut), EMPTY (0 chars — tool name + params only). Model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, tool_choice:required, temp 0.

results_on_same_8_points.full_matchesGroundTruth: 3-4/8 (ran twice: 4/8 and 3/8 — deepseek is NOT deterministic at temp 0, so single-point results carry ~±1 noise)

finding: First-sentence descriptions (93% smaller) match tool-selection as well as full descriptions (4/8 vs 3-4/8). EMPTY descriptions underperform (2/8) with clean per-point regressions where a bare tool name misled the model: turn 12 truth=read_file, empty picked list_files; turn 72 truth=write_file, empty picked run_python. Conclusion: the tool's FIRST SENTENCE carries the selection signal; the ~90% of prose beyond it does not; removing it entirely (empty) degrades selection. This single-prompt segment is the early-orientation phase (read vs list vs search) where descriptions matter MOST — exactly why empty lags here but ties elsewhere.
caveat: n=8, one task/model; deepseek temp-0 non-determinism moved the full baseline 3<->4/8, so the empty-vs-firstSentence gap (2 vs 4) is at the edge of noise but is corroborated by the concrete per-point regressions and by the earlier tests (first-sentence tied full at 7/12 on the multi-turn run and 6/6 on the synthetic tasks).
